Mutual Inductance Formula: Quick Reference Table

The mutual inductance formula you need depends on what you already know about the two coils. Use this table as a one look summary of the formulas covered above.

Known valuesMutual inductance formula
Self inductances and couplingM = k √(L1 × L2)
Induced voltage and current changeM = V2 ÷ (dI1/dt)
Flux linkageM = N2 × Φ21 ÷ I1
Two coils on a common coreM = μ0 μr N1 N2 A ÷ l
Series aiding and opposing testsM = (L aiding − L opposing) ÷ 4

Units: M is in henry (H), L1 and L2 in henry, k has no unit and lies between 0 and 1, A is in m² and l in metres.

Example: two coils of 4 mH and 9 mH with k = 0.5 give M = 0.5 × √(4 × 9) = 0.5 × 6 = 3 mH.
